title: Turborepo or Nx
dek: Both now call themselves the build system for coding agents. Under the shared tagline they are different tools. Turborepo is a small task runner and content-addressed cache on top of package-manager workspaces. Nx is a project-graph platform with plugins, generators, governance rules, and a paid CI fleet. This report compares them as they stand in October 2026. It covers how each sees a repository, what goes into a cache key, what each one costs, and a small benchmark of the two on the same twelve-package workspace.
byline: 2 October 2026 · Synthesised from turborepo.dev, nx.dev, both changelogs, and the npm and GitHub registries; timings measured on this machine with turbo 2.11.6 and nx 23.2.1
description: A sourced comparison of Turborepo and Nx as of October 2026: graph models, cache keys, remote caching, distributed CI, polyglot support, governance, agent features, pricing and supply-chain history, plus a benchmark of both on one synthetic workspace.
og_description: Turborepo 2.11 and Nx 23.2 side by side. How each models a repository, what goes into the cache key, Vercel Remote Cache versus Nx Cloud, distributed CI, polyglot plugins, generators and boundaries, agent features, pricing, and a measured benchmark on one twelve-package workspace, including a misconfiguration that silently ships stale builds.

How to read the badges

from the docs marks a fact from turborepo.dev, nx.dev, a release post, a pricing page, or the npm and GitHub registries (read 2 October 2026). measured here marks a number produced by the scripts in _bench/ beside this page, on a 2-vCPU Linux machine. The ratios carry over to other machines; the absolute milliseconds do not. reconstruction marks a judgement or mechanism I have worked out rather than read. Neither product's paid tier was exercised.
